findings.reason: The diff at lib/yargs-parser.ts:984 drops the boolean-negation guard, so negatedBoolean (line 112) is always passed to hasFlagsMatching. The parse branch at line 253 still requires configuration['boolean-negation'], so with negation off, '--no-foo' counts as known and is parsed as 'no-foo' instead of going to '_'.
findings.claim: isUnknownOption treats negated flags as known even when boolean-negation is disabled, so with unknown-options-as-args those flags are parsed instead of passed through to '_'.
findings.evidence: The diff removes `if (configuration['boolean-negation']) patterns.push(negatedBoolean);` and replaces it with `return !hasFlagsMatching(arg, flagWithEquals, negatedBoolean, normalFlag)`. hasFlagsMatching (line 936) returns true if any pattern's capture is a known flag, so '--no-dice' matches negatedBoolean (line 112), captures 'dice', and is classed as known. The negation branch at line 253 still requires `configuration['boolean-negation']`, so the arg is never actually negated; it falls through to the plain long-flag handling and sets 'no-dice'. Before the change, negatedBoolean was only checked when negation was enabled.

findings.reason: Neither reviewer reports a locked test that combines 'boolean-negation': false with 'unknown-options-as-args': true, and C2 cites test/yargs-parser.mjs:2536 as the only negation-off case. I didn't search the suite myself, so the gap isn't confirmed. Either way it's a test-coverage gap rather than a defect in the change itself.
findings.claim: No locked test covers boolean-negation off together with unknown-options-as-args on, so the regression passes the suite.
findings.evidence: The diff touches only lib/yargs-parser.ts. In test/yargs-parser.mjs, the only `'boolean-negation': false` case (line 2536) does not set 'unknown-options-as-args', and none of the unknown-options-as-args tests (lines 3047-3447, 4148+) disable boolean negation.
